FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
Hold the wheel at three and nine or at eight and four, never at ten and two or hands-on-twelve where airbags deploy [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
An average Virginia year brings over 100,000 reported crashes with over 900 deaths and over 60,000 injuries [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
Speeding ranks among the top crash and fatality causes, claiming about one-third of traffic deaths, and a 40 MPH crash is ten times more likely to kill than one at 20 MPH [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
At 60 MPH, striking a guardrail, pole, or parked car hits like a solid wall, and at 30 MPH a three-foot object drives almost three feet into the car [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
Obey every posted and unposted limit while checking local ordinances, weather, road conditions, construction, and school zones [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
Where no sign posts a limit, the maximums are 55 MPH on interstates and other public roads, 35 MPH on unpaved roads, and 45 MPH for school buses [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A02
The posted limit can still be unsafe: slow for rain, fog, traffic, rough pavement, poor night vision, and construction zones [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A02
When traffic moves faster than you, move over or match its safe pace; never crawl so slowly that you block normal flow [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A02
Every stop spans thinking distance plus braking distance, and at 55 MPH and beyond both run long as reaction travel grows with speed [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A02
Wet pavement doubles stopping distance, while packed snow or ice stretches it up to ten times dry length [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A02
Never stop where it endangers you or other drivers, and heed every no-stopping restriction [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A02
Never pass a school bus while it loads or unloads: flashing red signals and the extended stop sign both command a full stop [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A02
Stop for a loading or unloading school bus from either direction unless a separation or median divides the road; school buses themselves never top 45 MPH [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A02
Near playgrounds expect posted 15 or 25 MPH limits and slow for children who may dart out [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0017]
